title: isdiag
summary: Determine whether a matrix is diagonal in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: RunMat gathers gpuArray inputs and evaluates the diagonal predicate on the host.

description: `isdiag(A)` returns true when every nonzero element of matrix `A` lies on the main diagonal.
behaviors: Rectangular matrices can be diagonal when every off-diagonal entry is zero.
All-zero and empty matrices are diagonal.
Dense real, logical, complex, sparse, and gpuArray inputs are supported.
Complex entries count as nonzero when either real or imaginary part is nonzero.
NaN values count as nonzero when testing matrix structure.
Arrays with a non-singleton dimension beyond the second return `false`, matching MATLAB matrix-predicate behavior.

faqs.question: Does `isdiag` require a square matrix?
faqs.answer: No. A rectangular matrix is diagonal when all entries off the main diagonal are zero.

faqs.question: How are sparse matrices handled?
faqs.answer: RunMat scans stored sparse entries without densifying and returns false only when a stored nonzero appears off the main diagonal.

faqs.question: Does `NaN` count as zero?
faqs.answer: No. A NaN entry is treated as nonzero for structure predicates.

gpu_residency: RunMat gathers gpuArray inputs to host memory for this scalar predicate and returns a host logical scalar.
gpu_behavior: `isdiag` is registered as a structure-analysis fusion sink. GPU-resident inputs are gathered transparently before the host predicate runs, so explicit `gather` calls are optional.
